messages:
jamal: quick check — can someone run a medium soak/replay tomorrow morning (US-PST) against staging? saw a 2x bump in 99p on the canary after the recent kv-cache change. want to replay last week's traffic snapshot (~3h) and capture flamegraphs + k6/locust raw traces.

maria: I can take it if timing works. what's the target rps and exact snapshot id? also do we want k6 or locust for this one? k6 better for ramp control, locust for complex user flows.

jamal: thanks. target ~900 rps peak, 10m ramp, 3h steady. snapshot id is traffic-snap-2026-03-10:v3 (contains mix of chat/generate + embeddings). prefer locust for the replay-mapper flows, but k6 for simple burst scenarios. main ask: reproduce the 99p latency regression and capture py-spy flame every 5m.

alex: fyi the canary that regressed is built from commit 7a1b3f2 (release/2.1.4). I ran a quick bench on a smaller window and saw tail latency creep with larger request batches. attaching tiny log: ``ERROR: kv cache miss spike count=124, backend=redis-01``

maria: plan: I'll spin a dedicated pool in staging (4 x A100), preload snapshot via replay-mapper v0.3, run locust with the mapping file and enable --prefix-cache. command i'll run: ```./replay-mapper apply --snapshot traffic-snap-2026-03-10:v3 --out mapping.json
locust -f locustfiles/replay.py --headless -u 600 -r 30 --run-time 3h --csv soak_run``` 

jamal: add these extras if possible: set KV_CACHE_PREFETCH=1, enable prefix cache, and start py-spy: ```py-spy record -o /tmp/flame_$(date +%s).svg --pid $(pgrep -f 'redwood-runtime') --interval 0.05 --subprocesses``` capture every 5m slices. also collect per-route token breakdown from observability.

lee: tagging infra. I'll reserve the pool and pre-warm disks. note — disk iops for the snapshot prefetch was the blocker last time, so i'll attach an SSD pool and bump prefetch concurrency to 16. Also schedule 2026-03-18 09:00 PST as the default window unless someone objects. :calendar:

infra-bot: deploybot: staging pool "soak-2026-03-18" created by lee — 4x A100, 2TB NVMe attached, network egress quota checked.

alex: quick code-review ping — i left a small comment on the kv-cache PR about batching semantics, might explain the miss spike. tagging @maria so you can coordinate the repro after the PR change lands.

maria: ack. i'll coordinate with alex on the PR patchset; will run an A/B — with and without PR — to isolate. will post results + flame svgs here. :thumbsup:

jamal: perfect. only ask: when you post results include 50/95/99/99.9 latencies and ops/sec + a small table of config bits (batch size, prefix-cache, prefetch). if we see the regression we can try reduced batch sizes or a kv client fix asap.

lee: noted. I'll also enable a short-lived debug trace (1m) at 11:00 PST during the steady window to grab tcpdump if needed — will redact PII.

maria: thanks all — i'll start prepping the mapping job today and drop a final run-plan by EOD. if anyone wants to hop on the short run-call tomorrow 08:30 PST ping me.

jamal: thanks team. if we repro, we should consider an emergency hotfix for kv-client batching — low-risk change to fallback to smaller batches.

infra-bot: reminder: soak-2026-03-18 pool scheduled for 2026-03-18 09:00 PST. use channel #eng-runtime for updates.
